title: Selling Your Home in Greater Montréal

chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
Selling your home for the best price is not luck — it is method. The right list price, preparation, marketing, negotiation and follow-through to signing all matter. This guide gives you the game plan a broker uses to maximize price and minimize stress.

You will know what to do, in what order, and why — with the local realities of the Greater Montréal market.

After each chapter, a full-page lined 'My Notes' section helps you prepare YOUR sale.

chapters.title: Steps 1-2: the right price and preparation
chapters.objective: Start on solid ground: fair price and a market-ready home.
chapters.html:
Start on solid ground: fair price and a market-ready home.

Step 1 — Set the right price

The list price is the most strategic decision. Too high and the home stalls, goes stale and ultimately sells for less; too low and you leave money on the table. Price from a comparative market analysis (recent comparable sales), not a wish.

Step 2 — Prepare the property

  • Declutter, deep-clean, depersonalize.
  • Minor repairs that catch the eye.
  • Light home staging to showcase the spaces.
Le conseil d'Émilie

An overpriced home almost always sells for less in the end: it becomes 'the one that lingers.' The right price on day one creates the interest that drives offers up.

chapters.title: Steps 3-4: marketing and showings
chapters.objective: Expose the property to the most qualified buyers.
chapters.html:
Expose the property to the most qualified buyers.

  • Professional photos, video, a polished description.
  • Broad distribution (Centris, social media, broker network).
  • Make showings easy: availability, constant tidiness, owners away.

The first weeks matter most: that is when interest peaks. A well-prepared, well-priced home often gets its best offers early. Today the first visit happens on a screen, so quality photos are the highest-return investment of the whole sale.

Le conseil d'Émilie

Never skimp on photos. A well-prepared home that is poorly photographed sells for less than it should.

chapters.title: Steps 5-6: offers and negotiation
chapters.objective: Turn interest into the best accepted offer.
chapters.html:
Turn interest into the best accepted offer.

Evaluate each offer as a whole: price, conditions (inspection, financing), dates, and the strength of the buyer's financing. The highest offer is not always the best if its conditions are shaky.

  • Analyze price AND certainty.
  • Negotiate or counter while keeping your objective in mind.
  • In multiple offers, a fair, transparent process maximizes the result.
Le conseil d'Émilie

Do not be dazzled by the number alone. A slightly lower but near-certain, well-financed offer can be worth more than a high, fragile one.

chapters.title: Step 7: from acceptance to closing
chapters.objective: Secure the sale through to signing.
chapters.html:
Secure the sale through to signing.

An accepted offer is not a closed sale: conditions remain (inspection, buyer's financing, document review). Good follow-through keeps the deal from derailing in this sensitive window.

  • Facilitate the inspection and access to documents.
  • Provide the notary with required documents (certificate of location, seller's declaration).
  • Prepare your own move and key handover.

Remember: in Québec the seller's declaration and the legal warranty matter — disclose known defects honestly to reduce the risk of post-sale disputes.

Le conseil d'Émilie

Stay collaborative while conditions are being met: a well-supported transaction reaches the finish line. That is where a broker's experience makes the difference.

chapters.title: Plan d'action
chapters.html:
Vos prochains pas, concrètement.

Cette semaine

  1. Get a comparative market analysis to set the right price.
  2. Begin decluttering and minor repairs.

D'ici 30 jours

  1. Arrange professional photos and marketing.
  2. Organize flexible, well-prepared showings.

Ensuite

  1. Review offers with Émilie and secure the transaction to the notary.

chapters.title: Ressources & lexique
chapters.html:
• Comparative market analysis: recent comparable sales used to price the home.
  • Home staging: presenting the home to sell faster and for more.
  • Seller's declaration: form disclosing what the seller knows about the property.
  • Legal warranty of quality: protects the buyer against hidden defects.
  • Certificate of location: surveyor's document, often required to close.
